:::{.theorem data-title="Zero-One Law"}

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the smallest $\sigma$-algebra of subsets of $\Omega$ which
contains a collections $\{A_{n},~ n\geq 1\}$ of events. If for every
$n \geq 1$, $A \in \mathcal{A}$ is independent of $\{A_{i},~i=1,\dots,n\}$,
then either $\mathbb{P}(A)=0$ or $\mathbb{P}(A)=1$.

:::

*Intuitively, the result states that certain events must have probability 0 or
1 and no intermediate value, for example either something happens infinitely
often or it doesn't.*
